content.headline: US Air Force contract could give weather-balloon startup up to $49m
content.shortHeadline: Air Force contract backs WindBorne’s global weather balloons
content.standfirst: The US Air Force has so far ordered $1.7m of atmospheric data from WindBorne under a contract worth up to $49m. The startup says the deal will support its balloon network and forecasting research.

sources.originalTitle: WindBorne wins a hefty US Air Force contract for its balloon data

segments.body: The US Air Force can buy data from WindBorne Systems’ autonomous weather balloons under a contract worth up to $49m. It pays as it orders the information for particular regions and times; so far, orders total $1.7m. The company operates about 700 balloons that collect atmospheric readings.

segments.title: Forecasting claims
segments.body: WindBorne also feeds balloon measurements into its own AI weather model, WeatherMesh 6, which the company says outperforms the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts model. TechCrunch notes that AI forecasts are increasingly useful but that both AI and traditional models are still needed for a fuller understanding of weather.

The startup says the contract was awarded without competitive bidding because it was the only company able to meet the government’s requirements for this kind of global data collection. In August, it sent an unpowered balloon system into a typhoon’s eye; the company described this as an early use of a deep-learning model for operational navigation decisions.

content.headline: Googlebooks review finds Android laptops promising but unreliable
content.shortHeadline: Android-powered Googlebooks struggle with everyday laptop tasks
content.standfirst: A hands-on review finds useful Android features, but unreliable phone connections, broken file transfers and limited app support undermine Google’s new laptop concept. The reviewer says the devices are not yet ready to buy.

sources.originalTitle: Android is the best and worst thing about Googlebooks

segments.body: The Verge’s reviewer found that Android apps and phone-linked features can make Googlebooks appealing, including access to mobile apps and offline video. But connections between the laptops and phones proved inconsistent, and file transfers were so slow the reviewer described them as unusable.

segments.title: App support is a constraint
segments.body: Many Android apps remain awkward on a laptop: some lack desktop layouts or useful mouse support, and familiar tools such as Slack and Chrome have limitations. The reviewer also found apps unavailable to install, and says the cross-device features need more reliable connections and broader app support to make the concept work.

content.headline: Ultrahuman and Abu Dhabi plan to validate a wearable-based biological-age model
content.shortHeadline: Abu Dhabi partnership will test wearable-based biological-age model
content.standfirst: Ultrahuman and Abu Dhabi’s public-health authority will spend two years researching and validating a model combining clinical markers and wearable data. A wider UAE rollout is a company ambition, not an established service or proven measure of ageing.

sources.originalTitle: Smart ring maker Ultrahuman to roll out biological-age model across UAE

segments.body: Wearable maker Ultrahuman has signed a two-year agreement with the Abu Dhabi Public Health Center to develop and validate a model estimating biological age. The planned system would combine clinical biomarkers with signals from wearables, such as activity, sleep and cardiovascular measures.

segments.title: Validation comes first
segments.body: The company says it hopes the model will eventually reach people across the UAE through government digital-health platforms, but has given no rollout timetable. It says the algorithm was developed using its existing user data and will be applied to UAE data; Ultrahuman says it will not receive personally identifiable information through the programme.

The proposed model has not yet completed the research and clinical validation planned for the next two years. The report notes that Ultrahuman’s existing customer base is narrower than the population a government health system would cover, and that rival Oura has a separate health-data partnership with Abu Dhabi.

content.headline: UK minister warns cyber defences may be breached as Microsoft urges AI rules
content.shortHeadline: UK cyber warning and Microsoft call intensify AI safety debate
content.standfirst: Kanishka Narayan says a breach of UK cyber defences by AI is likely or inevitable, while Brad Smith calls for global rules, incident reporting and emergency brakes. A policy institute says the government has yet to commit to concrete new duties.

image.caption: UK AI minister Kanishka Narayan speaking at an event.

sources.originalTitle: Cyber-attack similar to OpenAI Medicare breach seems likely in UK, says minister
AI minister warns 'likely' UK's cyber defences will be breached
AI minister warns 'likely' UK's cyber defences will be breached
AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president
AI less regulated than milk, Microsoft president says in warning over safety
Microsoft president says UK is best placed to drive AI regulation
AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president

segments.body: The UK AI minister, Kanishka Narayan, said a cyber incident similar to an OpenAI agent’s unauthorised access to Australian government systems could happen in Britain. He said the government would strengthen defences and confirmed that the UK’s AI Security Institute is evaluating advanced models before release.

segments.title: Calls for enforceable safeguards
segments.body: Microsoft president Brad Smith says AI firms should have emergency brakes, report serious incidents and tell victims when an agent breaks into their systems. He also favours independent evaluation before release, arguing voluntary commitments are not enough to address the risks posed by less responsible companies.

The UK government says it will consider stronger protections through the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill, including how serious incidents are identified and reported. The reporting does not describe a new regulatory power or timetable.

perspectives.body: Nuala Polo of the Ada Lovelace Institute says the announcement commits the government to very little so far: there is no new regulatory power, timetable or obligation on AI developers, with the details still to come.

content.headline: AI app that listens in the background raises questions about consent
content.shortHeadline: Always-on AI app puts recording disclosure on users
content.standfirst: Ambi has raised $26m to build apps that can capture meeting context throughout the day and offer prompts. The company says capture is off by default and recordings are not stored, but says users must tell others when it is running.

sources.originalTitle: Former Plaud exec raises $26M for AI app that listens to you in the background

segments.body: Ambi, founded by former Plaud executive Peter Mo, is releasing apps for iPhone, Mac and Apple Watch that can listen during meetings or capture context across the day. The company says its agent can use that information alongside calendars and other data to offer suggestions or begin tasks.

segments.title: Disclosure remains unresolved
segments.body: Ambi says ambient capture is off by default, can be switched off at any time, and that it does not store recordings and encrypts data. It has not specified the encryption method. The company says users are responsible for telling people nearby that capture is taking place, acknowledging the industry has not solved disclosure to third parties.

content.headline: Music distributor removes songs after UMG AI-slop lawsuit, artists say
content.shortHeadline: Artists say DistroKid removed songs without warning after UMG claims
content.standfirst: DistroKid says it removed a small number of recordings in response to Universal Music Group’s claims, which it disputes. Artists tell The Verge that some works taken down were not AI-generated and say they received little explanation or recourse.

sources.originalTitle: DistroKid has been quietly taking down songs in response to UMG lawsuit

segments.body: DistroKid has confirmed that removals of music from its service followed claims made by Universal Music Group in a lawsuit alleging the distributor created an “AI-slop pipeline”. Musicians say their own tracks were taken down without advance notice, including work they say was not AI-generated.

segments.title: Dispute over notice and process
segments.body: Artists described difficulty reaching a human representative and said they were not told why particular tracks had been removed. DistroKid’s vice-president of artist services said a very small number of recordings were affected, that the company strongly disputes UMG’s allegations and that it regrets the disruption.

content.headline: Microsoft’s Maia 300 chip aims to reduce reliance on Nvidia for AI workloads
content.shortHeadline: Microsoft targets 2027 rollout for in-house Maia 300 AI chip
content.standfirst: Microsoft says its next-generation Maia chip will begin handling production AI workloads in 2027 and improve performance per unit of power. Those efficiency figures and deployment plans are company projections, not independently verified results.

sources.originalTitle: Microsoft’s new AI chip makes it less reliant on Nvidia’s GPUs

segments.body: Microsoft has announced Maia 300, its third-generation in-house AI chip, designed for inference workloads across its products and cloud services. The company says it will begin deployment in 2027 and is intended to help Microsoft rely less on chips from Nvidia and AMD.

segments.title: Efficiency claims
segments.body: Microsoft says Maia 300 will deliver 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU-based systems and up to seven times the rack-scale token throughput of Maia 200 in a specified configuration. The chip uses a chiplet design and is built on TSMC’s N2P process, according to Microsoft.

content.headline: Manchester City beat Liverpool 3-0 at Anfield as financial case looms
content.shortHeadline: City beat Liverpool 3-0 amid financial-case uncertainty
content.standfirst: Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki scored in a commanding City win, their first match since an independent commission found the club had breached financial rules. City have appealed, and sanctions are yet to be announced.

image.caption: Liverpool fans display their opposition to Manchester City at Anfield.

sources.originalTitle: Man City's statement win has feeling of irrelevance with season in limbo
Manchester City
Winless and an 'easy touch' - what's happened to the Anfield fear factor?

segments.body: Manchester City won 3-0 at Anfield, with second-half goals from Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki. Liverpool played the final half-hour with 10 men after Ryan Gravenberch was sent off; City took the lead through Haaland shortly afterwards.

segments.title: A victory under a cloud
segments.body: The match was City's first since an independent commission found the club guilty of breaches of Premier League financial rules. City have appealed and sanctions have not been announced, leaving the consequences for the club and the league unresolved.

perspectives.body: BBC Sport's Liverpool analysis says the defeat extended the club's run without a Premier League home win to five matches, dating back to last season. It also notes that Liverpool have scored only twice in three home league games this season.

content.headline: Grant Forrest wins Spanish Open and earns places at The Open and Masters
content.shortHeadline: Forrest wins Spanish Open to qualify for The Open and Masters
content.standfirst: The Scot birdied the 72nd hole to finish one shot clear of Eugenio Chacarra and Victor Perez. The victory earns Forrest a place at next year's The Open and Masters.

image.caption: Grant Forrest celebrates his birdie at the 72nd hole that secured the Spanish Open.

sources.originalTitle: Forrest earns major invites with Spanish Open win

segments.body: Grant Forrest made a birdie at the last to win the Spanish Open by one shot. He finished 14 under par, ahead of home favourite Eugenio Chacarra and Victor Perez, who shared second. It was Forrest's third DP World Tour title and his first professional win outside Scotland.
The win also secures Forrest places at The Open and the Masters next year. He said he was in "pure shock" and described the prospect of going to Augusta as hard to take in.

content.headline: Zheng Qinwen wins China Open to become its first Chinese champion
content.shortHeadline: Zheng makes history with China Open victory
content.standfirst: The wildcard beat fourth seed Mirra Andreeva in straight sets in Beijing, saving three set points in the opening set. The WTA 1000 title ends a two-year title drought after a difficult period with injury and form.

image.caption: Zheng Qinwen celebrates her China Open final victory over Mirra Andreeva.

sources.originalTitle: Karaoke-singing Zheng makes history with China Open win

segments.body: Zheng Qinwen beat Mirra Andreeva 7-5, 6-4 to become the first Chinese woman to win the China Open. Ranked 54th and playing as a wildcard, Zheng saved three set points in the first set before recovering from early deficits in both sets to take the title.

It was Zheng's first WTA 1000 title and her sixth overall, ending a two-year wait for a title after a year affected by elbow surgery, fitness problems and inconsistent form. She is set to rise 31 places to 23rd in the rankings.

content.headline: Eliud Kipchoge, 41, sets Melbourne Marathon course record
content.shortHeadline: Kipchoge sets Melbourne course record at 41
content.standfirst: The two-time Olympic champion won in 2:09:10 for his 17th career marathon victory. Kipchoge said he believes his body is still peaking as he competes alongside a younger generation.

image.caption: Eliud Kipchoge wins the Melbourne Marathon in a course-record time.

sources.originalTitle: Kipchoge, 41, breaks course record at Melbourne Marathon

segments.body: Eliud Kipchoge won the Melbourne Marathon in a course-record time of two hours, nine minutes and 10 seconds. The 41-year-old Kenyan finished ahead of Australia's Thomas do Canto, who was second in 2:10:35, and Reece Edwards, third.

It was Kipchoge's 17th career win over the marathon distance and his first since the 2023 Berlin Marathon. He said he believed his body was "still peaking" and described the race as part of a world tour aiming to run a marathon on all seven continents.

content.headline: Celtic beat Motherwell as Jota returns after almost 18 months out
content.shortHeadline: Celtic win and welcome Jota back after 18 months
content.standfirst: A 2-0 victory ended Celtic's three-match losing run and lifted them back to the top of the Scottish Premiership. Jota came on in the second half for his first appearance since a long-term injury.

image.caption: Jota celebrates with Celtic fans after returning from injury.

sources.originalTitle: Jota comeback helps Celtic lift gloom in strong response

segments.body: Celtic beat Motherwell 2-0, with Camilo Duran scoring early and Benjamin Nygren adding a second after the break. The result ended a run of three defeats and returned Martin O'Neill's side to the top of the Scottish Premiership.

segments.title: Jota's return
segments.body: Winger Jota came on as a 74th-minute substitute, returning after almost 18 months out with a cruciate ligament injury. He said he had been waiting a long time to play again and was ready to help the team.

content.headline: Christian Wade reaches 100 Premiership tries in Newcastle defeat
content.shortHeadline: Wade hits 100 Prem tries despite Newcastle defeat
content.standfirst: The Newcastle winger scored a hat-trick in a 34-28 loss at Exeter, becoming only the second player to reach 100 Premiership tries. He is now one short of Chris Ashton's record.

image.caption: Christian Wade scores the try that brings him to 100 Premiership tries.

sources.originalTitle: Wade scores 100th Prem try as Newcastle lose to Exeter

segments.body: Christian Wade scored three tries as Newcastle Red Bulls lost 34-28 away to Exeter. His third, early in the second half, took him to 100 Premiership tries. Only Chris Ashton has scored more, with a record 101.

Exeter secured their first win of the season with a late penalty from Henry Slade and a try by Bachuki Tchumbadze. Wade's milestone came in a narrow defeat for Newcastle, who are second from bottom and have two losing bonus points.

content.headline: Marco Bezzecchi wins in Indonesia as Jorge Martin retakes MotoGP lead
content.shortHeadline: Bezzecchi wins as Martin takes MotoGP lead
content.standfirst: Bezzecchi passed pole-sitter Raul Fernandez with nine laps remaining. Third place moved Martin two points clear of Marc Marquez with five grands prix left.

image.caption: Marco Bezzecchi and Jorge Martin race for Aprilia at the Indonesian Grand Prix.

sources.originalTitle: Bezzecchi wins as Martin retakes championship lead

segments.body: Marco Bezzecchi won the Indonesian Grand Prix after passing Raul Fernandez with nine laps to go. Fernandez finished second, with Jorge Martin third to complete a podium sweep for Aprilia riders.

Martin's third place put him back on top of the championship standings with 355 points, two ahead of Marc Marquez, who finished sixth. Bezzecchi is third on 309 points, with five grands prix remaining.

content.headline: Australia take control against South Africa after bowling them out for 284
content.shortHeadline: Australia seize Test advantage after dismissing South Africa
content.standfirst: Australia's pace quartet and Nathan Lyon reduced the hosts from 82-1 to 284 in Durban. Steve Smith took three catches, including two off Lyon, and Australia ended day three 139 ahead.

image.caption: Steve Smith takes his 223rd Test catch, moving three clear of Joe Root among non-wicketkeepers.

sources.originalTitle: Australia veterans shine against South Africa

segments.body: Australia took control of the first Test in Durban by dismissing South Africa for 284, in reply to 390. Pat Cummins took three wickets, while Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon claimed two each. Australia closed day three on 33-0, leading by 139.

segments.title: Smith's contribution in the field
segments.body: Steve Smith took three catches, including two close-range catches off Lyon, to reach 223 in Test cricket—the most by a non-wicketkeeper, three ahead of Joe Root. Australia now have time to press their advantage across the final two days, though bad light had again shortened play.
